title: Serviceability Life Assessment
subtitle: ML-driven structural degradation prediction across Tokyo, LA, Kolkata & Guwahati
description: A cross-city machine learning pipeline that models how environmental exposure — humidity, seismic activity, monsoon cycles, freeze-thaw stress — accelerates structural degradation in reinforced concrete. Trained on condition survey data from four cities with distinct climate profiles to build a globally-transferable serviceability life prediction model.

evolution.title: Research Genesis
evolution.description: Identified a gap: serviceability life models are mostly city-specific. Wanted a model that transfers across climates.

evolution.title: Dataset Architecture
evolution.description: Curated degradation survey data from Tokyo (seismic), LA (dry heat/seismic), Kolkata (tropical monsoon), Guwahati (flood-prone). Defined 24 environmental exposure features.

evolution.title: Multi-Climate ML Model
evolution.description: Building a gradient-boosted regressor + LSTM hybrid for time-series degradation curves. City as a categorical feature with climate embeddings.

evolution.title: Dashboard & API
evolution.description: Interactive web dashboard for engineers to input structural parameters and receive serviceability life predictions with confidence intervals.

evolution.title: IS Code Integration
evolution.description: Map outputs to IS 456:2000 serviceability limit states and generate automated maintenance schedule recommendations.

problemsFaced: Survey data from different cities uses inconsistent rating scales — harmonisation required
Tokyo and LA data is abundant; Kolkata and Guwahati data is sparse
Seismic exposure is a binary event but its effect on degradation is continuous and lagged
failedAttempts: First attempt: train a single global model on raw features — terrible out-of-city generalisation
Tried one-hot encoding city — model memorised city averages instead of learning patterns
lessonsLearned: Climate embedding via K-means on weather features generalises much better than city labels
Degradation is non-linear — tree ensembles outperform linear regression by 38% MAE
Data from 10 buildings in one climate is worth more than 100 buildings in same climate
futureWork: Add satellite-based carbonation depth estimates as a passive monitoring input
Explore transfer learning from Japanese structural health datasets
journal.notes: This project exists at the exact intersection of what I study. Civil engineering provides the domain knowledge to make the ML meaningful.

buildAnalytics.breakdown: AI assists with model architecture experiments and data pipeline boilerplate. Domain expertise — knowing what features matter structurally — is entirely manual.

title: Quizify
subtitle: LLM-powered PDF-to-quiz engine using Gemma 4
description: An agentic application that ingests complex exam PDFs — technical manuals, academic syllabi, IS codes — parses them using Gemma 4 via the Gemma API, and generates contextually accurate multiple-choice and short-answer quizzes. Designed to handle domain-specific language in engineering and data science curricula.

evolution.title: Exam Prep Problem
evolution.description: Tired of manually creating practice questions from IS codes and IIT Madras study material. Decided to automate it.

evolution.title: LLM Selection & Prompting Strategy
evolution.description: Evaluated Gemma 4, Claude Haiku, and GPT-4o-mini for technical domain accuracy. Gemma 4 won on domain-specific terminology retention.

evolution.title: PDF Parser + Quiz Generator
evolution.description: Building the structured output pipeline: PDF chunking → Gemma 4 question generation → difficulty classification → Next.js interactive UI.

evolution.title: Self-hosted + Public Beta
evolution.description: Deploy as a Vercel + FastAPI stack. Open to classmates at JU and IIT Madras.

evolution.title: Spaced Repetition Engine
evolution.description: Add an SM-2 spaced repetition scheduler to turn Quizify into a full active recall study system.

problemsFaced: PDF parsing of multi-column academic papers loses structural context
Gemma 4 occasionally hallucinates answer choices that sound plausible but are subtly wrong
IS code PDFs contain tables and diagrams that raw text extraction misses
failedAttempts: PyPDF2 for parsing — completely mangled column layouts in technical papers
Direct prompt: 'generate 10 questions from this text' — quality was poor on first attempt
lessonsLearned: pdfplumber + custom table extraction handles IS code layouts far better
Chain-of-thought prompting with explicit difficulty scaffolding massively improves question quality
Structured output with JSON schema prevents Gemma from drifting off-format
futureWork: Add image understanding for diagram-based questions
Multi-user sessions with shareable quiz links
journal.notes: Building tools you actually use teaches you what matters. This is already saving me study time.

buildAnalytics.breakdown: Heavy AI assistance for the LLM integration patterns and Next.js boilerplate. Prompt engineering, domain-specific evaluation, and the study pedagogy design are entirely manual.

title: GIS-Based Flood Risk Mapping
subtitle: Remote sensing + ML for flood vulnerability analysis
description: An automated pipeline that ingests satellite imagery and DEM data to produce flood risk maps using terrain analysis and machine learning classification. Integrated with QGIS for visualization and field validation workflows.

evolution.title: Initial Concept
evolution.description: Identified the need for automated flood risk assessment after studying manual surveying limitations.

evolution.title: Research & Planning
evolution.description: Reviewed literature on remote sensing-based flood mapping. Defined dataset requirements and processing pipeline.

evolution.title: Pipeline Development
evolution.description: Building the satellite data ingestion, DEM processing, and ML classification modules.

evolution.title: QGIS Plugin
evolution.description: Package as a QGIS plugin and build a lightweight web dashboard.

evolution.title: Real-time SAR
evolution.description: Integrate Sentinel-1 SAR data for near-real-time flood detection.

problemsFaced: Google Earth Engine API rate limits
60% of Sentinel-2 images unusable due to cloud cover
failedAttempts: Landsat 8 — too coarse for urban flood mapping
First Random Forest overfit on zero-flood tiles
lessonsLearned: SAR data penetrates clouds — far superior for active flood mapping
Stratified sampling essential for imbalanced classes
journal.notes: This project is teaching me more about data quality than about ML. The engineering fundamentals matter more than the algorithm choice.

buildAnalytics.breakdown: Core algorithm design, GIS methodology, and validation are manual.

title: Structural Load Optimizer
subtitle: Python-based beam and slab load distribution tool
description: A command-line and Streamlit web tool that computes load paths, bending moments, and shear force diagrams for simple beam and slab configurations using stiffness matrix methods.

evolution.title: Course Assignment Origin
evolution.description: Started as a structural analysis assignment. Decided to build a reusable tool.

evolution.title: Scope Definition
evolution.description: Limited to simply supported beams and one-way slabs.

evolution.title: Core Engine
evolution.description: Implemented stiffness matrix methods and Matplotlib-based SFD/BMD plotting.

evolution.title: Streamlit Web App
evolution.description: Wrapped in Streamlit for interactive use.

evolution.title: 2D Frame Analysis
evolution.description: Extend to full 2D frame analysis with IS 456 code checks.

problemsFaced: Numerical instability in stiffness matrix for near-zero element lengths
failedAttempts: SymPy for symbolic math — too slow for real-time updates
lessonsLearned: Numerical methods need careful boundary condition handling
Streamlit has real limitations for complex state
journal.notes: First project where I felt the connection between theory and code. The moment diagrams matching textbook answers felt genuinely satisfying.

buildAnalytics.breakdown: Almost entirely manual. AI only used to generate docstrings.
